questions.prompt: What does information security protect?
options: Only the computers that are switched on
Information and the systems that hold it
Only the cables and routers of a network
Only the passwords that users type in

questions.prompt: How does information assurance go further than information security?
options: It means the data can never be changed by anyone
You can trust it is protected, correct and there
It removes the need for passwords on every system
It protects only the data that is stored on paper

questions.prompt: In security, what is an asset?
options: The chance that harm will happen
Someone who could cause harm to data
Anything valuable you must protect
A weakness that an attacker can use

questions.prompt: A hacker, a virus and a flood are all examples of what?
options: Policies
Threats
Controls
Assets

questions.prompt: A default password that was never changed is an example of what?
options: An asset
A compensating control
A threat
A vulnerability

questions.prompt: What is risk?
options: A person who tries to break into a system from outside
Any device on the network that holds important data at all
A rule that says how people may use the systems
The chance a threat uses a weakness, and how bad

questions.prompt: Which part of the CIA triad means only the right people can see the data?
options: Non-repudiation
Availability
Confidentiality
Integrity

questions.prompt: Someone secretly changes a grade in a school database. Which part of the CIA triad is broken?
options: Availability
Integrity
Confidentiality
Accountability

questions.prompt: A flood of traffic takes a website offline. Which part of the CIA triad is broken?
options: Integrity
Availability
Confidentiality
Non-repudiation

questions.prompt: How many parts of the CIA triad does every attack break?
options: All three
Exactly two
At least one
None of them

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a vulnerability and an attack?
options: An attack is someone using a weakness
A vulnerability is someone using an attack
An attack is a weakness that nobody has found
They mean exactly the same thing in security

questions.prompt: What are default credentials?
options: The username and password a device ships with
A login that only an administrator can use
The last password a user typed by mistake
A password that the user picked for themselves

questions.prompt: Why do attackers try default passwords first?
options: They only work after midnight
Many systems never change them
They are written on every login page
They are always very long and strong

questions.prompt: What makes ethical hacking different from a crime?
options: Permission from the system's owner
Working only during the day
Using only free hacking tools online
Testing only very old systems

questions.prompt: What is the first stage of a typical attack?
options: Hideout
Recon
Data-grab
Entry

questions.prompt: In the hideout stage, what does an attacker usually set up?
options: A patch for the bug they used
A firewall to keep defenders out
A backup of the victim's data
A way back in, like an account

questions.prompt: You find one stage of an attack in a log. Why look for the others?
options: The first stage deletes all the others
Attacks only ever have a single stage
The other stages are probably nearby
Logs always show every stage in order

questions.prompt: Which part of an attack is most worth finding after the break-in?
options: The entry, because it cannot be closed
The hideout, because it stays open
The data-grab, because it is already over
The recon, because it was the first step

questions.prompt: What is phishing?
options: A cable tap that copies network data
A program that floods a server with traffic
A weak password that is easy to guess
A fake trusted message meant to trick you

questions.prompt: An email comes from "astro@c0dexia.lan" instead of "astro@codexia.lan". Which tell is this?
options: A spoofed sender
A strong password
Urgency
A firewall rule

questions.prompt: "Reset your password right now or lose access!" Which phishing tell is this?
options: Urgency
A signed email
A spoofed sender
A safe link

questions.prompt: Why does phishing get past strong technical defenses?
options: It turns off every antivirus program it finds
It uses a faster cable than the firewall checks
Firewalls only block messages sent on weekends
It targets a person's judgment, not the network

questions.prompt: Why is security awareness training management's job too?
options: Training makes the firewall run faster every day
Managers are the only ones who receive any email
People who spot phishing stop what tech can't
Training replaces the need for any passwords

questions.prompt: What is an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP)?
options: Written rules for how people use the systems
A list of every device on the network
A firewall rule that blocks games
A program that scans every single file for viruses

questions.prompt: The AUP says "no shared logins", but three people share one. What is true?
options: The rule protects nobody until it is enforced
The AUP must be deleted and written from scratch
Shared logins are safe if all three are on the crew
The rule protects them because it is written down

questions.prompt: Which behavior breaks a typical AUP?
options: Changing a default password
Logging in with your own crew account
Running a game on a shield console
Locking a confidential file

questions.prompt: A CONFIDENTIAL file is readable by anyone logged in. What is the fix?
options: Rename the file so nobody finds it
Print it out and delete the copy
Move it to a bigger hard drive
Limit it to the people who need it

questions.prompt: What is the hard part of a security policy?
options: Printing it and putting it on the wall
Writing the first draft of the rules
Making it true everywhere it is broken
Choosing a title for the document

questions.prompt: Which of these is an asset for the crew?
options: A weak password
A power cut at night
A Doom hacker
The starmap data

questions.prompt: A stolen laptop exposes customer records. Which part of the CIA triad is broken?
options: Confidentiality
Non-repudiation
Availability
Integrity
